skills.name: alert-investigation
skills.description: Investigates a firing or recently fired observability alert: finds the firing and replays the value it evaluated, decides whether the alert is chronic noise or a new problem, reuses any automatic investigation, then finds the cause (what changed, which host, version or route is over-represented) and returns a structured diagnosis with cause, scope and next steps.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: apply
skills.description: Apply LaunchDarkly SDK onboarding: install dependency (or dual-SDK pair), configure env and secrets with consent, add init at entrypoint(s), verify compile. Nested under sdk-install; next is run.

skills.name: built-in-metrics
skills.description: Instrument an existing codebase with LaunchDarkly config tracking. Walks the four-tier ladder (managed runner → provider package → custom extractor + trackMetricsOf → raw manual) and picks the lowest-ceremony option that still captures duration, tokens, and success/error.
skills.compatibility: Requires the LaunchDarkly server-side AI SDK (`launchdarkly-server-sdk-ai>=0.20.0` for Python or `@launchdarkly/server-sdk-ai>=0.20.0` for Node) and an existing config.

skills.name: configs-create
skills.description: Create and configure configs in LaunchDarkly. Helps you choose between agent vs completion mode, create the config, add variations with models and prompts, and verify the setup.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: configs-targeting
skills.description: Configure config targeting rules to control which variations serve to different users. Enable percentage rollouts, attribute-based rules, segment targeting, and guarded rollouts.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server. Scripted setup without MCP needs an API access token with ai-configs:write permission.

skills.name: configs-update
skills.description: Update, retire, and delete LaunchDarkly configs and their variations. Use when you need to modify config properties, change model parameters, update instructions or messages, take unused configs out of service, or permanently remove them.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: configs-variations
skills.description: Experiment with configs by creating and managing variations. Helps you test different models, prompts, and parameters to find what works best through systematic experimentation.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: create-fix-pr
skills.description: Investigates a root cause and files a minimal fix PR for a reported bug or observability finding.
skills.compatibility: Requires git and the GitHub CLI (gh); pairs with the investigate skill

skills.name: create-graph
skills.description: Creates observability dashboards and graphs from logs, traces, errors, sessions, metrics, and events data by previewing charts inline and saving them to a dashboard.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: custom-metrics
skills.description: Create, track, retrieve, update, and delete custom business metrics for configs. Covers full lifecycle: define metrics with the LaunchDarkly MCP server, emit events via SDK, and query results.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server to create and read metrics. Updating or deleting a metric needs a LaunchDarkly API token with the `writer` role. SDK examples use `launchdarkly-ai-server` 0.3.0+ (Python) or `@launchdarkly/ai-node` 0.3.0+ (Node.js).

skills.name: detect
skills.description: Detect repository stack for LaunchDarkly SDK onboarding: languages, frameworks, package managers, monorepo targets, entrypoints, existing LD usage. Nested under sdk-install; next is plan.
skills.compatibility: Requires access to the project repository

skills.name: experiment-orchestration
skills.description: Takes a product goal through a LaunchDarkly experiment and, if it wins, a guarded rollout (or a regular rollout on plans without guarded rollouts). Uses GitHub for the code change and deployment when it is connected to the agent space; otherwise hands those steps to a person.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server in an AWS DevOps Agent space. GitHub is optional.

skills.name: flag-and-release-change
skills.description: Drive a pull request's change end to end: decide it's flag-worthy, create the guarding flag, wire the new code path behind it on the PR branch, and record an automated release so the change ships safely when the PR merges. A portable orchestrator that composes should-flag-change, launchdarkly-flag-create, and flag-release. Keywords: flag a PR, wrap change in a flag, dark launch, kill switch, auto-release, automated rollout, end-to-end flag workflow.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server and a git CLI with access to the PR's repository

skills.name: flag-release
skills.description: Record an automated rollout for an existing LaunchDarkly flag that guards a pull request's change, so the change releases safely when the PR merges. Honors a stated release intent (release now / hold / notBefore / segment / prerequisite) and otherwise releases each environment with its default environment release plan. Use as the release step once the guarding flag exists and its code is wired. Keywords: record release, automated rollout, release plan, default release plan, flag release plan, guarded rollout, progressive rollout, release intent, hold release, dark launch.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server. Operates on a flag that already exists; does not create flags or edit code.

skills.name: investigate
skills.description: Finds the root cause of a production problem from observability data (logs, traces, errors, sessions, metrics): scope and onset, what changed (deploys and flag changes), which host, version, route or flag variation is over-represented against a baseline, then trace, log and error evidence and blast radius. Use when the user reports a bug, an outage, an error or latency spike, an incident, or asks about patterns across application data.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-automations-archival-settings
skills.description: Read and change a LaunchDarkly project's Automations auto-archival settings via the hosted MCP. Auto-archival archives flags that are ready to archive after a grace period, or creates approval requests for them. Use when the user wants to see or change the grace period, approval requirement, run limit, recheck cadence, or notification recipients, turn automatic archival off or on, or asks why a flag was or was not archived automatically. For first-time setup of every Release Autopilot capability, use launchdarkly-release-autopilot-onboarding.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-automations-cleanup-settings
skills.description: Read and change a LaunchDarkly project's Automations auto-cleanup settings via the hosted MCP. Auto-cleanup runs on a schedule and opens pull requests that remove the code for flags that are ready. Use when the user wants to turn automated flag cleanup on or off, change its schedule, repositories, flag states, job limit, or agent instructions, see which flags the next run will pick up, or asks why cleanup did not open a pull request. For first-time setup of every Release Autopilot capability, use launchdarkly-release-autopilot-onboarding.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-experiment-guide
skills.description: Guide a developer from 'I don't know what to test' to a ready-to-create LaunchDarkly experiment. Use when someone wants to run an experiment or A/B test but doesn't have a metric, a flag, or a hypothesis yet, or isn't sure what to measure. Scans the codebase and the connected LaunchDarkly account, proposes a hypothesis and metric from real context, wires up the flag and tracking code, then drafts the experiment and offers to create it. Built for engineers without a data-science or product-analytics background.
skills.compatibility: Uses the LaunchDarkly MCP server when it is configured; otherwise falls back to the LaunchDarkly REST API (needs a LaunchDarkly API token). Reads the local codebase and git history.

skills.name: launchdarkly-experiment-hypothesis-builder
skills.description: Help a user turn a rough idea into a strong, testable experiment hypothesis, or grade one they already wrote. Scores the draft against the Change / Measurement / Rationale rubric, scaffolds an If/then/because sentence with fill-in questions for what is missing, and detects junk input, A/A tests, and multiple measurements. Coaches in conversation, or returns the experiment builder's JSON contract when the caller asks for JSON only. Can check existing flags and metrics with read-only lookups, then hands off to launchdarkly-experiment-setup. Never writes to LaunchDarkly.
skills.compatibility: Works without tools. When the LaunchDarkly MCP server is connected, uses read-only lookups only. Hands off to launchdarkly-experiment-setup for anything that creates or changes a resource.

skills.name: launchdarkly-experiment-setup
skills.description: Set up and run experiments in LaunchDarkly. Create experiments with metrics, treatments, and flag config, start iterations to collect data, swap design between iterations, and stop with a winner.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-flag-cleanup

skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-flag-command

skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-flag-create

skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-flag-discovery

skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-flag-drift

skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-flag-qualitative-feedback-setup

Use when the user wants to add a Give Feedback widget, collect user sentiment tied to feature flags, set up feedback collection, or wire up the $ld:feedback tracking event.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-flag-targeting

Use when the user wants to change who sees a flag, roll out to a percentage, add targeting rules, or promote config between environments.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-guarded-rollout

skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-metric-choose

skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-metric-create

skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-release-autopilot-onboarding
skills.description: Step-by-step onboarding wizard for LaunchDarkly Release Autopilot: pick capabilities (auto-flagging, auto-releasing, auto-cleanup, auto-archival), connect the GitHub App, map repositories to projects, choose which AI model account runs the agents (LaunchDarkly's by default, or your own Anthropic or OpenAI key), set up environment release plans (with starter plans) and the project's flag release plan, and turn on scheduled flag cleanup and archival. Use when the user wants to set up, onboard to, preview, or continue setting up Release Autopilot. For a single settings change or 'why didn't my PR get classified?', use launchdarkly-release-autopilot-settings instead.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-release-autopilot-settings
skills.description: Configure LaunchDarkly Release Autopilot settings (GitHub App auto-flagging and auto-releasing) via the hosted MCP, or diagnose why a pull request was not classified / auto-flagged. Use when the user wants to turn on auto-flagging, map a GitHub repo to a LaunchDarkly project, change Release Autopilot account defaults, unmap a repo, or asks why Release Autopilot did not classify their PR. For first-time setup (pick capabilities, connect GitHub, choose inference, set up environment release plans and the project's flag release plan), use launchdarkly-release-autopilot-onboarding instead. For release plans, use launchdarkly-release-plans. For auto-cleanup or auto-archival settings, use launchdarkly-automations-cleanup-settings or launchdarkly-automations-archival-settings.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: launchdarkly-release-plans
skills.description: List, create, edit, make default, and delete LaunchDarkly release plans of both kinds: environment release plans (one environment's phases, rollout steps, and rollback metrics, with starter plans) and flag release plans (a project's environments in release order, each with its environment release plan, which Release Autopilot proposes releases from on pull requests). Also starts a flag's release from a flag release plan. Use when the user wants to see, build, change, or remove a release plan, set an environment's or a project's default plan, or when another skill such as Release Autopilot onboarding needs release plans planned or created. For first-time Release Autopilot setup, use launchdarkly-release-autopilot-onboarding, which follows this skill.
skills.compatibility: Environment release plans use the hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server. For flag release plans, and for deleting an environment release plan, the user runs the REST API (beta) commands that the skill shows in their own terminal.

skills.name: legacy-sdk-migrate
skills.description: Migrate an app from the legacy LaunchDarkly AI SDKs (Python `launchdarkly-server-sdk-ai` / `ldai`, Node.js `@launchdarkly/server-sdk-ai`) to the current handler-based AI SDKs (`launchdarkly-ai-server`, `@launchdarkly/ai-node` / `@launchdarkly/ai-server` plus handler packages). Use when code calls `LDAIClient`, `initAi`, `completion_config` / `completionConfig`, `agent_config` / `agentConfig`, `agent_configs`, `create_tracker` / `trackMetricsOf`, `create_judge`, `create_model`, or `agent_graph`, or when the user asks to upgrade between LaunchDarkly AI SDKs. For apps with hardcoded LLM prompts that aren't on LaunchDarkly yet, use `migrate` instead.
skills.compatibility: Python 3.12+ (`launchdarkly-ai-server` 1.0.0+ with `launchdarkly-server-sdk`) or Node.js (`@launchdarkly/ai-node` 1.0.0+). No LaunchDarkly MCP tools needed; the AgentControl configs already exist.

skills.name: mcp-configure
skills.description: Configure the LaunchDarkly hosted MCP server during onboarding. Use when the parent LaunchDarkly onboarding skill reaches the MCP offer, after the first flag works. Supports Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, and other MCP-compatible agents. OAuth authentication; no API keys for the hosted server.
skills.compatibility: Requires an MCP-compatible coding agent and a LaunchDarkly account

skills.name: migrate
skills.description: Migrate an application with hardcoded LLM prompts to a full LaunchDarkly AgentControl implementation in five stages: audit the code, wrap the call, move the tools, add tracking, attach evaluators. Use when the user wants to externalize model/prompt configuration, move from direct provider calls (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Gemini, Strands) to a managed config, or stage a full hardcoded-to-LaunchDarkly migration.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: observability-plugin-setup
skills.description: Set up LaunchDarkly observability for an app that already uses a LaunchDarkly SDK by adding the observability plugin to its existing client and opening a pull request. Use when an observability tool reports the project has never received data (observability_set_up or observabilitySetUp is false), when observability queries come back empty because nothing is instrumented, or when the user asks to add observability, error monitoring, logs, tracing, or session replay to a LaunchDarkly-enabled app.
skills.compatibility: Needs a codebase with an existing LaunchDarkly SDK client. Uses the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server to confirm data arrives.

skills.name: onboarding
skills.description: Scripted onboarding for LaunchDarkly: quiet execution, fixed sequence, SDK install, first flag with a live reveal, MCP offered afterwards. Enforces step completion before advancing and redirects drift. Use when adding LaunchDarkly, setting up or integrating feature flags in a project, SDK integration, or 'onboard me'.
skills.compatibility: Requires an MCP-capable coding agent and `npx` on PATH for optional skill installs. SDK keys, client-side IDs, and mobile keys are only needed when the SDK key step runs.

skills.name: online-evals
skills.description: Attach judges to config variations for automatic LLM-as-a-judge evaluation. Create custom judges, configure sampling rates, and monitor quality scores.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server. Scripted setup without MCP needs an API access token with ai-configs:write permission. SDK examples use `launchdarkly-ai-server` 0.3.0+ (Python) or `@launchdarkly/ai-node` 0.3.0+ (Node.js).

skills.name: plan
skills.description: Generate a minimal LaunchDarkly SDK integration plan from detected stack: choose SDK type(s), dual-SDK server+client when required, files to change, env conventions. Nested under sdk-install; follows detect, precedes apply.
skills.compatibility: Requires completed or equivalent detect context (see sibling detect skill)

skills.name: projects
skills.description: Guide for setting up LaunchDarkly projects in your codebase. Helps you assess your stack, choose the right approach, and integrate project management that makes sense for your architecture.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server. Code that creates projects itself (scripts, IaC, admin tools) needs an API access token with projects:write permission.

skills.name: sdk-install
skills.description: Install and initialize the correct LaunchDarkly SDK during onboarding by running nested skills in order: detect, plan, apply. Parent onboarding Step 4 is first flag.
skills.compatibility: Requires a supported language/framework in the project. SDK credentials are required by [Apply](apply/SKILL.md), not for [Detect](detect/SKILL.md) / [Plan](plan/SKILL.md) alone (see parent onboarding **Prerequisites**).

skills.name: should-flag-change
skills.description: Decide whether a given code change should be placed behind a LaunchDarkly feature flag. Use when a developer asks whether a change should be behind a flag, when reviewing a diff or pull request, or when running in CI on a PR. Reads the diff and surrounding code, then emits a structured advisory recommendation. Read-only: it never creates or modifies flags.
skills.compatibility: Advisory and read-only. Works on all platforms. Does NOT require the LaunchDarkly MCP server. Reads code with standard file tools (Read/Grep/Glob) and returns a structured verdict via the `recommend-flag` tool.

skills.name: snippets
skills.description: Create and manage prompt snippets — reusable text blocks referenced inside config variation prompts. Keeps common instructions, personas, and guardrails consistent across multiple configs.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server

skills.name: tools
skills.description: Give your agents capabilities through tools (function calling). Helps you identify what your agent needs to do, create tool definitions, and attach them to config variations.
skills.compatibility: Requires the remotely hosted LaunchDarkly MCP server. Application code examples use `launchdarkly-ai-server` 1.0.0+ (Python) or `@launchdarkly/ai-node` 1.0.0+ (Node.js).
